_comment: Codex wiring for the .agents/hooks/ module. Repo-scoped: active when working in a
repository that ships .agents/hooks/, and inert everywhere else.
The matcher is deliberately broad. Each hook re-checks the tool name against its own
precise set, so a matcher that catches more than it should cannot cause a false fire.
See .agents/hooks/README.md for the module contract.
Every command is an interpreter fallback, `python3 <hook> || python <hook>`, matching
what .claude/settings.json does and what .opencode/plugins/zen-hooks.mjs has always
done in code. A bare `python3` is inert on Windows, where that name resolves to the
Microsoft Store app-execution alias: a stub that advertises an install and exits
without running anything. bug-0050 measured that cost in the Claude Code wiring at 21
silent failures over three weeks; bug-0058 is the same spelling here.
Whether Codex runs these through a shell was NOT observed, and could not be: this
machine's 71 Codex sessions all predate the hooks module, so this file has never been
exercised. The change is safe without that observation, which is why it was made
anyway, and the argument is worth keeping because it is the reason and not a guess.
With a shell, `||` does what it says and Windows is fixed.
Without one, the command splits into argv and the tail arrives as arguments to the
script. No hook in this module reads sys.argv, so it behaves exactly as the bare
`python3 <hook>` did: measured 2026-08-31, `python <hook> || python <hook>` passed as
literal argv exits 0 and emits exactly one JSON object.
So the fallback is never worse than what it replaces, under either hypothesis. Note
that `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` in every command already assumes a shell, so a
Codex without one would mean this wiring is inert everywhere today rather than only on
Windows, and this change would still not be what made it so.
